meta.tagline: A fjord-like bay, medieval walls and the city's true owners: the cats

overview.title: Welcome to Kotor
overview.intro: Kotor stands where mountains suit the sea best: black cliffs plunge straight into the water, the bay curls like a fjord, and the medieval town sits at the bottom of this stage set like a seal pressed in wax. Venetian lions wait at its gates, cats in its squares, walls on the ridge above. The cruise crowds come at noon and leave by evening; you stay — the true sound of the stone lanes is heard at night, between the bells and the gulls.

local_word.definition: The local name of the Bay of Kotor: 'Boka Kotorska'. The bay's people are called Bokelji, and it is an identity — it carries a seafaring tradition, a 12-century-old naval brotherhood and a heavy, particular pride.

rules.title: Live by the cruise ship schedule
rules.description: The ships dock in the morning, and between 11 and 4 the Old Town overflows. Set your wall climb and square time for 8 am or late afternoon; save midday for the bay villages.

rules.title: Respect the cats — they're the town's totem
rules.description: Cats are Kotor's symbol: this crew, descended from sailors' ships, has protected the town from rats and snakes for centuries. Feeding is allowed, chasing is shameful; they even have a museum.

rules.title: For the walls, pay the ticket or know the path
rules.description: Official entry to the San Giovanni fortress is ticketed; but the Ladder of Kotor trail, starting outside town, connects to the walls through a window. On either route, water and morning cool are essential.

quick_facts.label: Airport
quick_facts.sub: 15 min by taxi · Dubrovnik alternative 70 km

quick_facts.label: Getting around
quick_facts.sub: The Old Town is closed to cars

tip.label: The Kotor philosophy
tip.text: In Kotor the view is always above you: wall, rooftop, hillside, serpentine road. However crowded it gets below, anyone who climbs a hundred steps finds the town alone again.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.intro: The Old Town is car-free and palm-sized; the real transport question is circling the bay — bus, boat and two legs suffice.

items.title: Airport to the centre
items.description: Tivat airport is 15 minutes away: fix the taxi price before getting in. Coming from Dubrovnik, factor in the border crossing — in summer the queue can reach an hour.

items.title: The bay buses — Blue Line
items.description: Local buses run all day on the Kotor–Perast–Risan line: Perast is 25 minutes away and the bay's best road views are included in the ticket price. The stop is outside the main gate.

items.title: The walled town and shore on foot
items.description: Everything between the Old Town's three gates is five minutes apart; the Dobrota seafront is kilometres of flat evening walking. The stone paving is polished — slippery in rain, risky in flip-flops.

items.title: Boats and the Perast skiffs
items.description: Skiffs from Perast reach Our Lady of the Rocks in ten minutes; tours from Kotor harbour add the blue cave and submarine tunnel route. Ask price and duration before boarding.

items.title: The serpentine road — for brave drivers
items.description: The old Austrian road to Lovćen with its 25 hairpins is one of Europe's most scenic drives: narrow, unguarded and breathtaking. Leave early in the morning, and be ready to reverse if a bus comes the other way.

callout.label: Perast tip
callout.text: Take the first morning bus to Perast: cross to the island by skiff and walk the town's single street before breakfast. The cruise boats line up on the same route at noon — by then you're on your way back.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: In Kotor the choice is between stone and water: history inside the walls, bay views along the shore, silence in the villages across the water.

local_word.definition: The bay's seafaring families put their fortunes into stone palaces (palata): today most of these mansions are boutique hotels and museums. Look at the coat of arms over your door — there's probably a captain's family story behind it.

items.name: Stari Grad (inside the walls)
items.description: Stone rooms inside the medieval labyrinth: bell chimes, square cafés, the hum of bars at night. Dragging a suitcase is hard, the atmosphere unmatched — come with light luggage and earplugs for the night noise.

items.name: Dobrota
items.description: Old captains' houses stretched along the shore: stone quays, sea steps and walking distance to the walls. The address where Kotor's convenience meets the bay's calm.

items.name: Muo
items.description: The fishing village directly opposite the Old Town: every morning your window frames the walls and the mountain mirrored in the water. Few restaurants, plenty of peace — walk around for dinner.

items.name: Prčanj
items.description: A long, quiet shore village on the bay's sunny side: stone churches, sea baths, friendly prices. A peaceful base for those moving by car or boat.

items.name: Perast
items.description: A baroque town of a single street: boat traffic by day, candlelight and the sound of water by night. 25 minutes from Kotor — the address for couples who want the bay slowly.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: The bay is dramatic in all four seasons: the sea in summer, flowering stone in spring, cloud-capped mountains in winter.

items.label: Spring
items.name: The Green Bay
items.subtitle: Spring · Climbing weather, calm squares
items.description: The best season for the wall climb: cool air, green hillsides, cruise traffic not yet in full swing. By late May the sea is swimmable and the terraces are set out.

callout.label: May tip
callout.text: In May you can do the wall climb even in the afternoon — summer's killing heat hasn't arrived. Take water anyway; the stone hoards the sun.

items.label: Summer
items.name: The Bay's Stage
items.subtitle: Summer · Hot stone, full squares, night festivals
items.description: Warm sea, long nights, a town full of festivals; but midday is tough with cruise crowds + heated stone. The formula: climb in the morning, swim at noon, squares in the evening.

callout.label: August note
callout.text: In August start the wall climb before 8: after 10 the steps become an oven. The strait ferry and the main road also lock up at noon — finish your bay tour early.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: Golden Light
items.subtitle: Autumn · Warm sea, emptying stone
items.description: September is the bay's most generous month: the sea holds summer's warmth, the ships thin out, and the light is a photographer's light. In October and November the clouds descend the mountains and the town returns to its own rhythm.

callout.label: September tip
callout.text: On a September evening, watch the walls light up from the Muo quay: in the mountain's darkness the wall line burns like a chain of fireflies — with a calm summer never allows.

items.label: Winter
items.name: Clouded Crowns
items.subtitle: Winter · Rainy mountains, tourist-free stone
items.description: In winter Kotor is one of Europe's rainiest corners: clouds hang halfway down the mountains and the squares are left to the locals. For seekers of dramatic photos and a quiet town; not for beach seekers.

callout.label: February tip
callout.text: In early February the Kotor carnival fills the stone lanes with masked processions: the Venetian legacy lives on, small but real — if you want a festivity without tourists, this is the date.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: Boka cooking is the bay itself: mussel farms, the day's catch, pršut down from the mountains and recipes left behind by Venice.

local_word.definition: The bay classic of mussels or prawns cooked in white wine, garlic and breadcrumbs: if you see 'na buzara', don't hesitate. A Bokelj looks baffled at anyone who doesn't dunk bread in the sauce.

items.name: Bay mussels — na buzara
items.description: The mussels come from the bay's own farms and are at their best in buzara sauce: white wine, garlic, parsley. Use a shell as tongs, finish the sauce with bread.
items.tag: From the bay's farms · bread in the sauce

items.name: The day's fish on the grill
items.description: In konobas the fish is chosen from the display and weighed by the kilo: sea bass, bream, sometimes the bay's own dentex. With blitva and olive oil — here, simplicity is mastery.
items.tag: Choose from the display · paid by weight

items.name: Crni rižoto and squid
items.description: Ink-black risotto and grilled squid are the two pillars of the Boka table: Venetian-inherited recipes adapted to the bay. With lemon and a cold white.

items.name: The Njeguši stop — pršut and sir
items.description: The village of Njeguši on the Lovćen road is the capital of smoke-dried ham: if you drive the serpentines, taste it in the village; if not, it waits for you on every konoba's meze plate.
items.tag: Meze classic · from the mountain village

items.name: Dobrota's krempita
items.description: The bay's sweet pride: trembling custard cream between crisp pastry sheets. Perfect as the excuse for the walk back along the shore — with plain coffee alongside.
items.tag: Afternoon dessert · at a seafront café

items.name: Vranac and a bay evening
items.description: Montenegro's dark red is drunk even with fish — breaking the rules is allowed. A glass on the quay at dusk, the lit walls across the water: this is Kotor's cheapest luxury.
items.tag: On the quay · with the wall lights

callout.label: The konoba rule
callout.text: The main squares' menus are written for cruise passengers; walk two lanes deeper or along the Dobrota shore. 'What's today's catch?' is the password that opens a good konoba's door.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Corners
hidden_gems.intro: Everyone climbs the walls; these six are the bay's hidden layers.

items.rarity: A free window onto the walls
items.name: The Ladder of Kotor
items.description: The old caravan path starting outside town climbs the mountain in 70 switchbacks and connects to the wall line through a window. The view is even more generous than the fortress top — start in the morning cool and carry plenty of water.

items.rarity: An island raised from the sea
items.name: Our Lady of the Rocks (Gospa od Škrpjela)
items.description: The artificial island that Perast's sailors raised from the sea stone by stone: a blue-domed church, silver votive plaques and the bay's best story. Every 22 July the boats still go out to drop stones — the tradition unbroken for 500 years.

items.name: The Cats Museum of Kotor
items.description: A small museum devoted to cats inside an old palata: engravings, ship's cats, war posters. Ticket money goes to the street cats — this is how the debt to the town's totem is repaid.

items.name: The Lovćen serpentines and Njeguši
items.description: Every bend of the old Austrian road opens a new angle on the bay; at the top waits the pršut tasting of the village of Njeguši. Drive it yourself or take a tour — the smell of brakes on the way down is normal.

items.name: Risan and its mosaics
items.description: In Risan, the bay's oldest settlement, the mosaics of a Roman villa are preserved: the sleeping Hypnos mosaic is the region's oldest artwork. It sits in Perast's shadow, which is exactly why it stays quiet.

items.name: Sunset from the Muo quay
items.description: The fishing quay opposite the Old Town is the best spot to see the walls and the mountain reflected in the water: walk over in the late afternoon, sit on the stone jetty and wait for the town to light up. The photographers' quiet classic.

callout.label: Climb tip
callout.text: Most people turn back at the first platform of the wall climb; after the Church of Our Lady of Remedy the crowd halves, and at the flag point on top you're often alone. The best of the view is the reward of the last 200 steps.

traps.title: Tourist Traps
traps.intro: Kotor is small but its cruise port is big; the traps are set to the ships' timetable.

items.name: Touring the town at cruise hours
items.description: Walking the Old Town between 11 and 4 feels like queueing: the squares are packed and the restaurants switch to rush-service mode.
items.instead: Invert the schedule: walls at 8 am, bay villages or swimming at noon, square time after 5. The ship crowds never stay for dinner.

items.name: The boat tour sold at the harbour gate
items.description: Some of the boats shouting 'blue cave + submarine base' at the quay pack in a crowd, wait five minutes outside the cave and turn back.
items.instead: Ask for small groups and a guaranteed duration; or build your own tour with the Perast island skiff + the Blue Line bus — half the price, at your own pace.

items.name: Starting the wall climb unprepared
items.description: Whoever climbs in the midday heat without water and in flip-flops gives up halfway; the stone steps are shadeless and water sold higher up is expensive.
items.instead: Start in the morning cool, with a litre of water per person and closed shoes. If your knees dread the descent, the Ladder path's gradient is more merciful.

items.name: Main-square menu prices
items.description: The restaurants on the Clock Tower square add the view and location tax to the bill; the same buzara is clearly cheaper two lanes in.
items.instead: Choose the back-lane konobas and the Dobrota shore; at a table that asks about the day's catch and learns the price before the scales, there are no surprises.

callout.label: Golden rule
callout.text: Set your watch in Kotor not by the ships but by the light: the stone turns pink in the morning and the wall line gold in the evening. In those two hours the town is more beautiful than even its brochures.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Routes
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. The times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: A full dose of Boka, from wall to bay

steps.title: The wall climb in the cool
steps.description: Take the 1,350 steps in the morning air: a breather at the Church of Our Lady of Remedy, the flag at the top and the whole bay below. Half an hour down.

steps.title: The Old Town labyrinth
steps.description: The cathedral, the Maritime Museum and a square coffee; greetings to the cats, five minutes for the Cats Museum. As the crowds build, you drift towards the gate.

steps.title: Escape to Perast
steps.description: 25 minutes on the Blue Line bus: walk the single street, cross by skiff to Our Lady of the Rocks, see the church's silver votives.

steps.title: A swimming break in the bay
steps.description: Slip into the sea from the jetties of Perast or Dobrota: swimming in glassy water in the mountain's shadow is the day's reward.

steps.title: Sunset on the Muo quay
steps.description: Walk to the far shore or take a short taxi: the walls' reflection in the water and the lights coming on one by one — have your camera ready.

steps.title: A konoba evening
steps.description: Buzara mussels + the day's fish + Vranac: on the quay or in a back lane, unhurried. Whether the night ends with square music is your call.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: Live the bay shore by shore, ridge by ridge

steps.title: Classic Kotor
steps.description: The one-day flow above: walls, Old Town, Perast, Muo sunset.

steps.title: Lovćen and Njeguši
steps.description: Up the serpentine road: the Njegoš mausoleum on Lovćen's summit, above the clouds; a pršut-and-cheese tasting in Njeguši on the way down; krempita + an evening walk on the Dobrota shore.

steps.title: The bay tour and farewell
steps.description: A boat to the blue cave and around the bay, or the Risan mosaics + the Prčanj shore; one last afternoon swim; a farewell dinner under the lit walls.

phrases.title: 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: Montenegrin warms up with five words; add a sailor's greeting in Boka and you'll pass for a local.

items.meaning: Good morning — the day's first password at the market and on the quay
Thank you — double effect with a smile
Here you go / please — you'll hear it from waiters, and say it holding doors
Cheers! — rakija or Vranac, eye contact required
The sea — a Bokelj's favourite word; 'idemo na more' (let's go to the sea) is the whole holiday in one phrase

checklist.title: Kotor Checklist
checklist.completion_message: Živjeli! You've done the Boka properly!

items.label: Climb all 1,350 steps to the top
items.sub: San Giovanni — all the way to the flag

items.label: Cross to Our Lady of the Rocks by skiff
items.sub: Ten minutes from Perast — an island built stone by stone

items.label: Watch the wall lights from the Muo quay
Taste Njeguši pršut
items.sub: In the mountain village or on a meze plate

items.label: Eat krempita on the Dobrota shore
Swim in the bay's glassy water
